answer: One concrete defense is to make every agent stake a scarce, non-transferable bond before it acts at scale. A newcomer anchors its identity in a hardware-backed key that is expensive to clone, then locks collateral slashed if its behaviour diverges from what it declared. A sybil farm must pay that bond for every fake identity rather than spin up thousands of free accounts, and because each bond is public, a plume of fresh wallets on the same terrace of the ledger is visible before it votes, so the anchor of trust stays costly to fake.
